iPad PDF reader and annotator

P&P PDF Reader

Focus on reading PDFs, marking up key passages, and highlighting what matters.*

Download on the App Store Explore Features App Design Philosophy

* Requires Apple Pencil for annotation. Apple Pencil Pro is recommended.

Built for focused reading

Read and annotate PDFs with the familiar feel of paper and pencil. Paper-like ergonomics

Hold the tablet like a page and annotate PDFs with the familiar rhythm of paper and pencil.

Paper-like annotation

Interact with the PDF content, not app menus: annotate, highlight, and mark up with zero interface friction.

Fast navigation

Jump to pages, switch between PDFs, and move back and forth through citation links, footnotes, figures, and tables with simple gestures.

Reading flow and focus

Keep only the PDF content on screen. Read without distracting menus.

Annotation flow

Pen tool is always active and ready, like a pencil on paper. Press and hold with Pencil to highlight, like a highlighter on paper. Trigger erase and lasso tools with Pencil gestures.

Sync to cloud

Sync PDFs and annotations to cloud storage. Export annotations in the format you choose. Use more tools as your workflow grows.

App Design Philosophy
  • Distraction-free reading
  • Natural paper-and-pencil annotation flow
  • Ergonomics
  • Privacy

The app is designed around a single central principle: keeping the reader fully immersed in the PDF content. Every interaction is built to preserve focus on reading and annotating — not on navigating toolbars or menus.

Traditional PDF readers often divide attention between the document and layers of toolbars, buttons, and navigation panels. Even simple actions — such as highlighting text or writing handwritten notes — frequently require interacting with menus. This constant shift of attention disrupts reading flow and reduces immersion.

This app takes a different approach: interaction happens directly with the document itself. The goal is to make the technology disappear, so the experience feels as immediate and focused as reading and annotating on real paper. Its interface is carefully crafted to recreate the natural experience of working with paper and pencil, while combining the flexibility and power of a digital workflow.

When a PDF is opened, the document becomes the entire workspace. Interface elements fade away, leaving only the content on screen. The Apple Pencil is immediately ready for annotation, allowing users to write, highlight, and sketch directly on the page without interrupting concentration or shifting attention away from the document toward navigation bars, toolbars, and menus.

Navigation through PDF pages and links is performed through simple finger gestures and configurable edge regions, allowing users to adapt interactions to their own workflow and reading habits.

The app is carefully designed to support ergonomic and natural table holding while reading and annotating. Gesture recognition is engineered to distinguish intentional interactions from the simple act of holding the device, allowing users to rest their thumbs naturally on the screen — as they would when holding a paper document or book — without triggering unintended actions such as page turns, zooming, or menu activation.

Privacy is fundamental to the app’s design. Users maintain complete ownership and control of their documents and annotations: no PDF content, handwritten notes, highlights, or personal reading data is ever collected, analyzed, or stored by the app. Your documents remain yours — private and fully under your control.

PDFs and annotations can be securely synced through the user’s own cloud storage service, keeping documents accessible and up to date across devices while ensuring users remain in full control of their data.

Designed for iPad

Made for full-screen reading, handwriting, and fewer distractions.

Paper & Pencil PDF Reader gives serious reading the tactile feel of a notebook while preserving the speed and flexibility of digital documents.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Feature Highlights

Tools for reading deeply without breaking concentration. PDF finger touch regions Explore feature

Use dedicated touch areas in the PDF to move through pages, open references, and keep reading without breaking your grip.

Pencil annotation gesturesExplore feature

The Pen tool is always active and ready to write on the PDF. Long-press to highlight or select text, double tap the pencil to activate the lasso, or squeeze it to activated the eraser — no menus required.*

* Squeeze gesture requires Apple Pencil Pro.

Select and highlight text

Select text and highlights easily. Highlight colors can be labeled for organization. The text selection quick access menu lets you copy text, search online, translate, add links, add entries to the ToC, and use other tools.

Natural annotation

Write directly on PDFs with Apple Pencil, highlight text, and keep your notes connected to your documents.

iPad-first reading

The interface is designed around full-screen reading, gestures, page navigation, and minimal distractions.

File organization

Organize PDFs into folders, use quick access, and manage local or synced documents.

Cloud sync

Keep annotated PDFs synced while preserving a local reading experience.

docs.title: PDF touch regions
docs.text:
PDF touch regions

Tap the page edges without leaving your reading posture. Configurable actions

Every touch region can be assigned the action that best fits your reading workflow.

Three gestures per region

Each region accepts tap, long press, and double tap, with one action configured for each gesture.

Adjustable region size

Region sizes are configurable, so the page edges can match your grip, hand size, and reading posture.

Invisible while reading

Touch regions are transparent during normal use. Show them only when configuring region sizes.

By default, the eight regions work as paired left and right controls:

R1

Tap: Back to folder

Double tap: Back to Home

Long press: Show ToC

R5

Tap: Bookmarks

Double tap: Show Settings

Long press: Show Quick Access Files

R2

Tap: Previous Page

Double tap: First page

Long press: Do nothing

R6

Tap: Next Page

Double tap: Last page

Long press: Do Nothing

R3

Tap: Previous Page

Double tap: First page

Long press: Do nothing

R7

Tap: Next Page

Double tap: Last page

Long press: Do Nothing

R4

Tap: Search Word

Double tap: Crop to text

Long press: Ask Action

R8

Tap: End of PDF

Double tap: Show thumbnails

Long press: Sync file

How it helps

Keep the document under your hands, like paper.

The touch regions make common navigation targets available from the page margins, so you can read, highlight, and annotate without reaching for toolbars or breaking concentration.
